glosses: The cardinal number occurring before one and that denotes no quantity or amount at all, represented in Arabic numerals as 0.

examples.text: The conductor waited until the passenger count was zero.
A cheque for zero dollars and zero cents crashed the computers on division by zero.

 These words of wisdom from the Dalai Lama might not have been in the minds of planners and engineers when designing new railway station platforms, but for several main line stations, zero is indeed something. Eight stations in the UK now operate a Platform 0 - from Cardiff to Kings Cross, Doncaster and Haymarket.

glosses: The numeric symbol that represents the cardinal number zero.

examples.text: In unary and k-adic notation in general, zero is the empty string.
Write 0.0 to indicate a floating point number rather than the integer zero.

glosses: The digit 0 in the decimal, binary, and all other base numbering systems.

examples.text: One million has six zeroes.

This effectively allows switching on and off of the flow of current, so it is either conducting or not conducting, creating the binary system of zeroes and ones used in digital computers.

glosses: Nothing, or none.

glosses: The value of a magnitude corresponding to the cardinal number zero.

examples.text: The electromagnetic field does not drop all of the way to zero before a reversal.

glosses: The point on a scale at which numbering or measurement originates.

examples.text: The temperature outside is ten degrees below zero.

glosses: A value of the independent variables of a function, for which the function is equal to zero.

examples.text: As the next example shows, the set of zeros may well have a limit point not belonging to the domain.
The zeroes of a polynomial are its roots by the fundamental theorem of algebra.
The derivative of a continuous, differentiable function that twice crosses the axis must have a zero.
The nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function may all lie on the critical line.

glosses: The additive identity element of a monoid or greater algebraic structure, particularly a group or ring.

examples.text: Since a commutative zero is the inverse of any additive identity, it must be unique when it exists.
The zero (of a ring or field) has the property that the product of the zero with any element yields the zero.
The quotient ring over a maximal ideal is a field with a single zero element.

glosses: A person of little or no importance.

examples.text: They rudely treated him like a zero.

glosses: A Mitsubishi A6M Zero, a long range fighter aircraft operated by the Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service from 1940 to 1945.

examples.text: The visit to Townsville was filled with nostalgia for me. I remembered very well staying there on June 8, 1942. I shared a room with a brave and friendly officer, Colonel Francis Stevens. Early the next morning we flew to Port Moresby in New Guinea, and from there we took off in separate planes. Colonel Stevens never returned from that flight; his plane was shot down by a Japanese Zero.

glosses: A setting of calibrated instruments such as a firearm, corresponding to a zero value.
A security which has a zero coupon (paying no periodic interest).

examples.text: The takeovers were financed by issuing zeroes.

glosses: Synonym of no.

examples.text: She showed zero respect.

examples.text: Élection nulle pour vice de forme.

glosses: Mauvais, de mauvaise qualité, sans intérêt, qui ne vaut rien.

examples.text: Parfois, quand tous ces grotesques tapaient à bras raccourcis sur la République, on voyait ses yeux rire sans que ses lèvres perdissent leur moue d’homme grave.
